content.thinking:
I'm planning the phoenix's pose and proportions, figuring out how its body, wings, and trailing tail feathers should be positioned so the tail just grazes the ground while the body stays elevated in a flying stance.

Now I'm sketching out the skeleton hierarchy, defining the spine chain from hips through chest, neck, and head with a parent-child joint structure to anchor the rest of the rig.

I'm working out the head and beak geometry next—placing eye joints and the jaw, then shaping the upper and lower beak as tapered sweeps with a gold color on the head bone, before moving on to placing the eye decals on the skull surface.

Now I'm planning the crest as several curled feather sweeps along the back of the head in orange and gold, and sketching the main body silhouette as a catmull sweep running from hips through the spine to the neck with varying radii, aiming for a red-and-gold cel-shaded paint scheme with a furred edge.

For the body surface detail, I'm thinking through feather texture cards—gradient leaf shapes in red, orange, and gold—scattered across the body with downward flow to simulate plumage, before moving on to wing construction.

Now I'm designing the wing structure with a shoulder-elbow-wrist bone chain spreading upward and outward in a V shape, then figuring out how flight feathers should fan from the arm: upward-outward near the wrist, downward-backward near the shoulder, extruded as leaf-shaped outlines painted with a red-to-gold gradient along their length.

I'm working out the geometry for each feather's orientation—width perpendicular to the feather direction, length along it—so I can layer the feathers into three rows (long primaries, secondaries, short coverts) at slightly offset depths to avoid z-fighting while keeping them visually stacked.

Now I'm sketching the leaf-like outline for a single feather, with curved edges and a pointed tip, and considering shifting the tip asymmetrically to give the feathers a slight banana-like curl rather than a flat, symmetric shape.

For the wings, I'm setting up joint chains for shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand with a "wing" role, so feathers can be rooted at parametric points along the arm path and oriented using the chain's position and bone data. I'm defining how each feather's outward angle should rotate from a downward-inward direction near the shoulder to an upward-outward direction near the hand, so the feather fan follows the natural sweep of the wing.

I want to tune the feather lengths so primaries near the hand are longest and shoulder feathers are shortest, but checking the resulting wingspan shows the bird coming out roughly 3.5 meters tall and wide, which feels too large relative to the body proportions. I'm adjusting the joint coordinates downward and inward to shrink the overall silhouette while keeping the wing's natural arc intact.

Defining feather color gradients...

Still writing feather paint logic...

I'm also checking that the paint area for all feathers stays reasonable, estimating roughly 50 feathers at about 0.12 square meters each across both faces.

For the gold tips, I'm adding a zigzag boundary using a toon-style offset function so the gold color blends into the crimson cel with a jagged edge rather than a straight line.

Now I'm planning the arm's leading-edge detail: gold armor plates shaped like diamonds placed at three points along each wing's arm chain, each topped with a glowing ruby gem, to mimic ornate dragon-wing armor.

I'm orienting those diamond plates along the arm's tangent direction so they sit flush against the tube surface, with the gem offset slightly further out, and also sketching a V-shaped gold gorget necklace at the chest using a symmetric curved path from shoulder to shoulder.

Now I'm figuring out how to drape that gorget sweep onto the body's actual surface so it doesn't clip through, since the chest geometry bulges outward more than my rough path accounts for, and placing a small ruby gem plate at the center of the V. Then I'm laying out leg joint points for a digitigrade bird-like leg chain (hip, knee, ankle, foot) with slight outward offsets per side for a dangling flight pose.

I'm defining the thigh and lower-leg feather coloring with tapering radius arrays and color bands transitioning from red to brown, then working out how to sweep the toes as separate digit chains branching off the foot joint, with claws capped at each tip.

Working out toe positions...

Now I'm figuring out the ankle anklet with a gem, using a lathe profile to form a gold cuff ring around the leg, considering whether a cylinder geometry would work better for the open-ended band.

Positioning the ruby gem glow near the leg joint, then moving to the tail: planning seven long flowing plumes from the rump trailing down and back, each defined as a bezier sweep from base to tip.

Working out the tail's bone chain and plume geometry, treating each plume as a flat, thin swept tube with width in x and thickness in z, with symmetric left-right spread and curling tips for a natural feathered look.

Still writing plume paths and colors...

Adding curled outer tip feathers...

Now I'm thinking through decorative gem plates for the tail plumes, placing gold diamond/ruby ornaments at specific points along the sweep with proper frame orientation, and considering how to rig the tail plumes to a bone chain for movement.

I'm defining the tail bone chain with three joint names and positions tapering down and back, then adding a second shorter layer of rump plumes for density, and setting up the wing chains with shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand joints parented to the spine's third segment.

For the neck and head, I'm chaining three neck joints curving upward and outward, then attaching the head to the final neck joint. For the chest plumage, I'm sketching a leaf-shaped SVG feather path with a layered fill approach, using a smaller inner leaf shape near the tip to simulate a gradient without relying on actual SVG gradients.

I'm defining three feather color variants (red-to-orange, orange-to-gold, gold-to-pale) using a clip-path technique where a zigzag band near the tip overlays a base rectangle, plus a central rib stroke for detail. Then I'm scattering around 150 small feather cards across the body surface in two passes -- one for frontal hits using gold/orange textures and another for the rest using red/orange -- with randomized size, lean, bend, and spin for natural variation.

Now I'm adding small cheek feather cards on the skull with a filter to avoid covering the eyes, while keeping most of the head painted with a cel-shaded fur edge gradient between gold and orange. For the neck, I'm planning two rings of outward-facing feather cards along the neck chain at different positions, using the chain's frame to orient each card so it flows downward naturally.

I'm also designing five crown crest plumes as swept-back tube curves rising from the skull's crown, varying their lateral offset and length to create a dramatic sweep, with gold-to-orange-to-red color banding and a tapering radius profile along each tube. The beak stays gold with a tiny nostril detail, and I'm skipping extra brow geometry since the eye decal already implies one.

Now I'm building the gold wing crescents by offsetting the arm's chain path upward and sweeping a thin gold band along it, then sweeping the arm tube itself with a tapering radius array in red, using the same catmull chain for both the skeletal bone and the skin. I'm positioning primary feather roots along this arm path, computing each feather's fan angle and direction vector per row using interpolated angle ranges and normalized offsets to lay them out realistically.

Working out feather orientation and layering next...

Checking that the geometry stays monotone across the range of curvature values so the smoothing doesn't accidentally cut across itself near the corners.

Now I'm setting feather widths for each row and working out the color gradients per row — dark-to-red with gold tips for row A, red-to-orange-gold for B, orange-with-gold-tip for C, plain red for D — and defining a paint function for each feather based on length and these color stops.

I'll use jointAt for the wing bone and set direction arrays as simple number triplets. For the gems, I'm planning ruby with a flat glow colour and gold with a cel-shaded metallic plate look, then tallying up the palette.

Writing wing plate geometry...

I'm attaching plates to joints along the wing bones, adding gold shoulder crescents, and placing gem-studded tail plates. I'm also checking that body, leg, and tail positions stay above the floor level, confirming the lowest points sit safely around y=0.03.

Now I'm shaping the skull sphere and positioning the eyes using spherical coordinates with amber iris decals that mirror across the left and right sides, then considering small side head plumes swept back from near the cheek.

I'm working out the beak geometry using bezier curves for both the upper beak (tapering gold, flat cel-shaded color) and the lower jaw, with corresponding joints parented to the head joint. I'm also planning the hips joint as the root spine joint and double-checking which imports I'll actually need to avoid typecheck errors.

Now I'm settling on a color palette with cel-shaded hex values for deep red, orange, gold, pale yellow, metal tones, and brown, and figuring out the necessary imports from the builder, math, path, texture, and toon kits before writing the actual bird geometry code.

Working out the feather paint function...

Now I'm sketching the wing builder, defining shoulder-to-tip curves on each side using catmull-rom splines and chain segments for the wing structure.

Writing feather row placement logic...

I'm confirming the x and y directions stay orthogonal, then working out the parameters for row A's feather chain — spacing, taper, and angle range that determine how far the wingtip extends.

Now I'm defining rows B, C, and D the same way, tuning each feather group's count, phase offsets, length curve, width, z-offset, and color palette so the wing layers blend from deep red at the base to golden tips.

I realize row D's z-offset would overlap the armor plates, so I'm dropping row D entirely and repositioning the plates to sit just outside row C, adjusting C's z-depth to .028 so it tucks behind the plates cleanly. Now I'm working out the leading-edge metal band as a swept path along the wing bone chain, then computing the plate positions and orientations by sampling the arm curve at several points and building local tangent-based frames to orient each plate.

I'm shaping the diamond-shaped plates and gems, sizing their offsets against the tapering arm tube radius so nothing floats off the surface, and giving the gems a flat glow material. Then I'm setting up the tail chain with three segments and a plume-generation function that builds feather-like shapes in layered rows, varying position, length, and droop based on distance from the tail's center.

Now I'm defining a tapered radius function for the plumes, shaping them to start wide near the body and taper to a sharp point at the tip, then setting cap styles and figuring out how to color them with a gradient-like threshold system based on position.

I'm counting out the tail plume arrangement—thirteen main plumes plus curls—and working out where to place small gem plates along the central plumes using sweep positions at specific parameter points.

For orienting the diamond plates, I'm figuring out a frame from the tangent direction so each plate aligns with the plume's curve rather than facing an arbitrary direction. Now I'm defining the leg chains for each side with hip, knee, ankle, and foot joints, then sweeping tapered radii and color bands along each leg.

I'm adding toe chains branching from each foot's tip, spreading several front toes at different angles plus a back toe, each with a short mid and end joint offset outward from the foot position.

Now I'm sweeping those toe chains with a tapered brown cross-section and adding dark claw spikes at the tip, angled slightly downward from the toe direction.

For the anklet, I'm placing a metal cylinder around the leg at roughly 70% down its length, using the leg's frame at that point for orientation, and adding a small octahedron gem offset slightly forward from the attachment point.

I'm scattering feather cards on the thighs filtered by height, then using a cel-shaded paint function to split the body's front and back into gold and red/orange color regions based on surface normals and a zigzag pattern along the body axis. I'm also scattering dense feather cards across the body surface, splitting front-facing hits into gold/orange tones and back-facing hits into red/orange/deep tones for layered coverage.

Now I'm making sure the gorget (chest plate) is built after the body cards so it isn't covered, filtering the front card scatter to exclude the neck/chest region where the gorget sits, leaving that area for painted fur edges and a planned neck ring instead.

I'm placing a gem plate at the gorget hit point with gold ring cards around the neck for a ruff effect, sized and angled so they don't carry joints or awkward tangents, then moving on to sketch out the crest and cheek plume sweeps on each side of the head.

Now I'm plotting the crest using bezier curves for each spike—varying height, base offset, and curl-back tip positions—so the crest rises up to about y=2.89 with a tapering radius profile along each curve.

I'm assigning each crest spike a color gradient from gold through orange to red and back, and double-checking that the sphere-based skull fits cleanly inside the base radius. Then I'm setting up the fur-edge shading on the head so the top reads gold while the face shades toward orange, using an up-facing normal reference.

Now I'm sketching out the body geometry — sweeping a catmull-rom spine path through varying radii to shape the chest and torso, tying it to a spine/neck bone chain, and sanity-checking the joint positions for hips, spine segments, and the jaw hinge.

I'm working out the head joint orientation and how eye decals get placed onto the skull surface using a raycast hit point with mirroring for left/right symmetry, while double-checking type compatibility for direction vectors and outline typing.

Now I'm sketching a small helper function that builds a perpendicular basis from a direction vector, verifying the math makes the two axes orthogonal, and noting the import path for the glow module.

I'm checking the toon module import, then verifying the tail plume geometry tapers to a zero-radius point cap exactly at the path's end so the tip sits correctly near y=0.03, while confirming the gem wrapping with glow and tallying up part counts like feather groups.

Now I'm writing SVG leaf texture generators with clipped paths, tip shading, and rib strokes for the card atlas, then setting up the card array with default colors and flow direction inputs.

For the leg thigh, I'm scattering hits along the sweep surface with minimum distance and filtering by position, assigning flow directions for feather cards. For the wing, I'm attaching plate extrudes using joint references at parameterized points along the bone, then finalizing the toe chain parented to the foot joint before writing everything out.
